With updates making the game more and more unplayable and the heavy reliance on framegen. Avoid this game at all cost.

The game still can't keep to a stable 60fps with a R7 5800X CPU, 6700XT GPU on med settings.
100% reliant on TAA so your options are fuzzy smears or insane jaggies. Disgusting.
No issues fixed months, years on from release date, appalling.

Don't buy this if you're on Linux or a Steam Deck. There's a good chance that while getting trying to get it to work, you will be flagged as malicious and locked out of playing the game you purchased for 24 hours at a time. Other than that, performance is awful eight months after launch, even with the recommended specs on Windows. The game has Denuvo which is blatantly anti-consumer and probably responsible for the above 2 issues.

There are other, smaller issues I could get into regarding the gameplay and story, but in all honesty they are not significant enough to have made a difference in my recommendation.

Incredible game. But this performance is not ok

Edit: At TU4, performance is still horrible

Do not enjoy the direction this series is going. I already kinda assumed the days of slow, methodical position-based combat days were in the past, but it seems like the devs just want to make DMC 6 at this point. The main story was mind-numbingly easy and the late game stuff (AT Arkveld, Gogmazios, etc) was just a blur of aoe-spectacle that lacked all the elements of monster hunter fights that made me fall in love with the series back in Tri. Not to mention the increase in price and poor performance. If you enjoy the direction this series is going, more power to you, but this will probably be the last new MH game I play.
It has the potential to be GOTY but lack of end game content, boring event, and really poor performance really ruined the experience.
Perfect balance of quick hunt in rise and immersiveness of worlds. Performance is better compared to launch release with minimal stutter

It isn't a flawless experience, but its not hard to see the love and detail that has been put into this game, even if it's occasionally hard to see that because you have 30 fps. Good game overall though, and definitely a big value win among AAA games these days.
this game was marketed as the next step in gaming but it sucks so hard it's so poorly optimized i hate it

I think this game is fantastic!
The developers really put a lot of effort into the updates, and they fixed all the problems I had with performance and endgame difficulty, which in my opinion were the main issues holding the game back :)

The game is in a great place right now, and the new expansion looks amazing. If you stopped playing before, I recommend giving it another try!
game runs fine now even on an external ssd connected with usb 3.2. Might get some model pop-in but mostly ignorable.

This game is just not for me, many people will love it and Im incredibly jealous of them. Maybe its because they neutered my weapons move set or maybe Im just a grumpy old man now and being over dramatic but spending 400hrs of spamming the circle button just has none of the magic of older titles. I can play Freedom Unite, 3U, 4U, GU, World and Rise for hours and not get bored, but for some reason I just cant stay longer than 1-2 hunts on Wilds anymore. Something just doesnt feel right about it.

I’ve logged 400 hours on the PS5 version, over 500 hours in Monster Hunter: World, and more than 1,000 hours in Monster Hunter 4 Ultimate, with additional time across other entries. I first got into the series with Freedom Unite and have been consistently engaged ever since.

Compared to its predecessors, the monsters in Wilds feel noticeably easier. I’m hoping Ascension delivers a stronger challenge. Even so, I’ve enjoyed Wilds enough to start a PC playthrough now that the major issues have been resolved.

I may not be the right one to do a review of this game, but from what little I've played I would definitely recommend putting up with the Tutorial and giving the actual game a chance. It runs beautifully on my PC, and I haven't had a single issue playing it. 

For those with Carpal Tunnel, avoid the fast and light weapons.

if you like monster hunter, you’ll probably really enjoy this game. if you beat Fatalis and want a very hard experience for veterans, this is not it. it’s very streamlined, even for base game... however, the combat is fun, the monsters are great, and weapons have depth. game can get challenging on later tempered versions.

unfortunately, the performance is absolutely horrible. the game runs poorly on mid-range hardware and lowering settings doesn’t help much because the game is so CPU heavy. visuals also look blurry out of the box, like Capcom smeared vaseline on my screen... but with some 3am research, tweaks, mods, you can get it looking and running better.

i’m definitely hooked, but it’s hard to recommend in its current state. might be worth waiting for the first expansion.

Game is good.

Performance is bad.

Only get this if you have 0 MH content left to play. (help me)
Very good game for newbie playing the series for the first time, but for me, this game is a bit too easy compare to other 2 new gen game, hope they will fix this in the DLC

The music, art direction, and gameplay are peak imo. Some of the most fun I've had playing with friends (we're all big Monster Hunter fans since World/Iceborne).

I love the ecology/speculative evolution aspect of the Monster Hunter games, and it feels like they really fleshed that out here. The environments and ecosystems feel alive and it's beautiful.

It had a rocky start, but after a series of performance updates and constant content additions, it has become very enjoyable for me.
The combat feels very fluid, and the monster designs are excellent once again. Compared to Monster Hunter: World, I definitely see it as an upgrade in many areas.
With the DLC now on the horizon, I recommend picking it up and reaching the endgame before the expansion releases.
Overall, I highly recommend it. Very enjoyable game.
Honestly shocked that such a high profile game like this releases in this state. You'd have to purposefully sabotage your game to make it run this badly.

After finally fixing many of the performance issues, I can confidently recommend Monster Hunter Wilds.

As someone who put over 3,000 hours into Monster Hunter: World and another 300 hours into Wilds on PS5, I decided to rebuy the game on PC to get ready for the upcoming DLC. At the time, that felt like a mistake due to the game's rough technical state.

Thankfully, things have improved significantly. Performance is much smoother now, and while I still experience the occasional crash, it's nowhere near enough to overshadow what makes this game great. The combat is excellent, the monsters are memorable, and the world is stunning to look at. If you were holding off because of performance concerns, it's finally in a state where I can recommend jumping in.
This game put the nail in the coffin for me on the idea of universal suffrage.

locks you in so many cutscenes and moments that just take away control, won't let you explore, the multiplayer function seems to have been made by somebody who has no friends and doesn't know how a game is supposed to function. This was supposed to be a movie but they made it a form of immense self harm also. if you like playing a game at all, run away.

I'm enjoying it, but the presence of Denuvo means that I cannot, in good conscience, recommend the game on anything less than very recent technology (RTX 40 series, Intel 13th gen, etc.)

To be honest, the game is just poorly optimized. I am able to achieve higher than 60 FPS on my own setup without frame generation, but I can still tell something is just not quite right. It runs worse than the betas did, but there's one word that easily explains this.

Denuvo. Denuvo is that word. Why is anyone still using this garbage?

If something changes on this front (I don't expect it will, Capcom is notoriously stubborn on this point) then I may consider changing this review.

Again, I am enjoying the game. But for the purposes of recommending this game to the wider public, I feel the need to leave this red so that people REALLY consider whether this is a worthwhile purchase for them.

After months of being released, unfortunately, the situation hasn't changed. The game still performs horribly. Until these issues are resolved, I cannot see myself playing it for more than a hunt or two, then waiting for the next Title Update.

I didn't want to jump on the negative review train, because while the performance isn't great, and they clearly released the game before it was ready, it's still really good and fun to play.
What made me change my mind was the soundtrack that they released today for 73 euros.

I cannot recommend spending 70 euros on a game that barely runs 60 fps on above than recommended specs at the lowest graphical settings. Pick it up if you have the specs and t goes in discount, otherwise don't.

with Gogmazios coming into the fray we have a new armor set that has two different armor set bonuses, the upgraded artian weapons that also have a set bonus attached to em, transcended gear that upgrades older gear and gives more deco slots, everything looks and feel far more viable making the grind everlasting. all and all i was worried for the game after omega came out put praise be our Gog has delivered and its starting to look really good, i encourage vets to come back and give it a try.

furthermore the lineup of monsters in this game is fairly good, some places have been overused and i would personally like to see everything get spread out more and some new areas to explore in the future.
the events that have come out since launch have been very fun and engaging.
unfortunately there is tracking monsters anymore like in world, you more or less just go on a quest and stumble into it.
the game explores alot of the old world tech and story.

additionally i have encountered very few performance bugs, since this updates has come out, i do hope we can get further support for lower and middle spec pcs but it is looking very hopeful. 

all and all its a pretty good game i would give it an 8/10 and hopefully i can change that rating in the future when we get more content and dlc as well as performance fixes for pc.

If I could, I would give a neutral.

Low rank is genuinely one of the worst gaming experiences I've ever had. Greater emphasis on the story is a lovely idea, but executed in a way that greatly disrupted the core gameplay loop. Skippable cutscenes do nothing if they are followed by unskippable pseudo-gameplay sections that introduce the new biomes but don't let you explore them. You can literally take your hands off your controller/kb+m and the game plays itself.

But as soon as LR is over and you get to actually play the game, it is amazing. Weapons feel great, the combat is incredibly smooth, the world is beautiful and monster designed are phenomenal. This is probably a great introduction to the series with many QoL changes.

Performance is bad, UI is bad and multiplayer system is convoluted. But it's still a great game. You just need to get through the first 12 hours :D

In spite of all the negative reviews placed on this title thanks to its prevalent performance issues, I bought Monster Hunter Wilds, and I do not regret this choice. Monster Hunter Wilds offers an incredibly emmersive gameplay environment on top of a smooth and enjoyable combat system, as is common among Monster Hunter games. Throughout my hours in the game I have yet to experience the aforementioned performance issues while playing on the high graphical preset. Note this might be due to my higher end components which I do see that the game is not accommodating to lower end devices. Some may not validate my opinion due to my prior experience in Monster Hunter games being a few hours dispersed between Worlds and Rise. In short, Wilds is an excellent game with an even more fantastic gameplay flow, and this is all topped off with its gorgeous environment.

Monster Hunter Wilds - The Game That Turns You Into a Monster-Slaying Disaster!

Monster Hunter Wilds is like if you took every “hold my beer” moment and turned it into a game.

Gameplay? I have my gripes with it, but overall I love it.

BUT:
I pre-ordered the premium deluxe edition of this game because somehow, I still had SOME faith in Capcom despite how horrendous the microtransactions were in Rise. That was a mistake, very little of the DLC being released is actually part of the cosmetic DLC pass. Sure, that's on me for not reading closer to see what was actually included with the pass, but the fact remains I blew $40 above base price and I'm still only getting scraps of the post-release DLC. I'm never buying anything above the base edition again, and I'll probably wait for sales for even that.

Also the performance is steaming garbage, but you all already know that.

Overall, MH:Wilds is in my opinion a fantastic game that treats its players like garbage. If I wasn't hooked by the fact that there are no other games that execute this concept on the same level, I'd drop it entirely.

Played every monster hunter since Tri and this one has the most enjoyable hunts by far in regards to how base releases go. Every monster hunter is mixed before it's huge expansion update. Happened with world, rise, and now wilds. The game is good.

Excited to play this game, but the poor performance has left me very disappointed.

You compare this game with Kingdom Come Deliverance 2, which released earlier in the month, and it leaves me feeling that this level of performance for a big release from a big company like Capcom is simply not acceptable.

I will update this review when Capcom has addressed and corrected the performance.
